From The Date Of Petition Till Realization.

Court Delivered The Following:

 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-insurance company, calling in question the judgment and award dated 19.02.2011, passed in M.V.C.No.2044/2005, on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal & First Additional Senior Civil Judge And CJM, Mangalore, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) seeking to reduce the quantum of compensation.

sentences.text:
On 22.11.2005 the deceased Melvin Mascarenhas was riding a Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-19/R-9765 from Konaje side towards Asaigoli, on the left side of the road slowly and carefully and when he was proceeding at about 4.00 p.m., near Ganesh Mahal Building at Konaje, the bus bearing registration No.KA- 19/B-6799 driven by its driver rash and negligently, and dashed against the motor cycle of the deceased and caused accident.
3.
Hence, a claim petition was filed by the legal heirs under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the deceased.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Rs.13,02,632/-, along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The Tribunal held respondent Nos.1 and 2 therein, liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials on record.
5.
The learned counsel for the appellant-insurance company submitted that the deceased is a bachelor aged 47 years old at the time of the accident and the claimants are aged between 46-56 years old.
Hence, the claimants are not dependent on the income of the deceased.

Therefore, the Tribunal has committed an error in granting compensation under the head 'loss of dependency', but the compensation has to be granted under the head 'loss to estate' by taking the savings of the deceased at 50%.
If the deceased had been alive, then his contribution to the family is not more than 50% of the income, as he intended to spend more on himself.
Therefore, submitted to deduct the 'personal and living expenses' at 50% and grant compensation under the head 'loss to estate'.

Therefore, prays to reduce the compensation by allowing the appeal.
6.
On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent justified the Tribunal's judgment and award and prays to dismiss the appeal.
7. In the present case, undisputed facts are that the deceased was 47 years old and bachelor.
The claimants are two brothers and two sisters.
It is stated that the sisters are unmarried, therefore whether the compensation can be granted under the head 'loss of dependency' is proper or not is to be considered.

The Tribunal has determined compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' and deducted 1/4th of amount towards 'personal and living expenses' of the deceased and accordingly calculated the compensation under the head 'loss of dependency'.
8.
In the present case, the claimants are all majors aged between 34-56 years, therefore strictly it cannot be construed that the claimants are depending on the income of the deceased.

However,
taking judicial notice of the fact that two sisters are younger to the deceased and are still unmarried.
Therefore, where there is family consisting unmarried sisters, then, brothers would be contributing some amount to the maintenance to the family.

9. The learned counsel for the appellant relied on the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of A. MANAVALAGAN VS A. KRISHNAMURTHY AND OTHERS1 (hereinafter referred Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd vs Miss. Emilian on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191698014/
3 to as 'Manavalagan' case for short).

entities.text: A. MANAVALAGAN VS A. KRISHNAMURTHY AND OTHERS1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd vs Miss. Emilian on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case of Manavalagan stated to supra, this Court had made several illustrations for considering grant of compensation and in case of bachelor and the claimants are not depending brothers and sisters.
It was illustrated and made as standard deduction as to deduct 50% amount as savings of the deceased and if the deceased was alive then 50% of the savings amount would be contribution to the family.
Accordingly, granted compensation under the head 'Loss Of Estate'.

10. At the same time, the Division Bench of this Court in the aforesaid case held that though the quantum of savings will vary from person to person, but there is a need to make standard deduction and accordingly made as standard deduction of considering the savings of 50%, but this savings of deceased bachelor is not in a fixed formula and this quantum of compensation varies from person to person.
As the savings would be influenced by his attitude, ILR 2004 KAR 3268 care of brothers and sisters.
Therefore, the savings need not always be at 50% in case of death of bachelor and where the claimants are brothers / sisters.
Therefore, this can be considered according to the numbers of brothers and sisters of the deceased and whether they are married or unmarried etc.
Therefore, in the present case, there are two sisters who are unmarried and younger to the deceased.

Therefore,
on taking a judicial notice of fact, the sisters may not be earning for the family.
Even though there is no evidence on the part of the claimants that sisters are earning or not but the fact remains that the savings would be more keeping in mind the future life also.
Where the age of the persons growing older and elder as years move on, therefore, the savings would be fluctuated.

11. Under these circumstances, where there are unmarried sisters and therefore judicial notice of the matter has to be taken that in future also there is no need to make savings of the income and that would be considered as 50% of the income.
Therefore, while granting 'loss of dependency' in the present case 50% of the savings ought to have been considered.
Therefore, the grant of compensation by the Tribunal under the head 'loss of dependency' is not correct.
Therefore, the compensation is granted under the head 'loss of estate' by considering 50% of income.

12. In the present case, the income of the deceased is to be considered as Rs.10,960/- per month,
50% of the savings is to be considered under the head 'loss to estate' and deceased was 47 years old.
The appropriate multiplier applicable as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Smt.Sarla Verma & Others. Vs.
Delhi Transport Corpn And Another2 is '13'.

Therefore, the compensation under the head 'Loss To Estate' shall be quantified as follows:
Rs.10,962 x 50% x 13 x 12 = Rs.8,55,036/- AIR 2009 SC 3104 - 10 - 13.
There are four brothers and sisters of the deceased.

Therefore, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Magma General Insurance Co. Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others3 and in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi4, the claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each under the head 'Loss Of Consortium including Loss Of Love And Affection'.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, Rs.1,60,000/- (Rs.40,000 x 4) is awarded under the head 'Loss Of Consortium including Loss Of Love And Affection'.
Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd vs Miss. Emilian on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191698014/
4 14.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has granted compensation of Rs.10,000/- each is awarded under the head 'Funeral And Obsequies Ceremonies' and transportation of dead body respectively.

15. Thus, in all the appellants/claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation as follows:
 Loss to Estate : Rs. 8,55,036/-
 2018 ACJ 2782  (2017) 16 SCC 680  - 11 -  (Rs.10,962 x 50% x 13 x 12 )
 Loss of Consortium : Rs. 1,60,000/-
 Funeral and Transportation : Rs. 20,000/-
 Expenditure (In tact)
 TOTAL : Rs. 10,35,036/-
16.

Therefore, the appellants-claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.10,35,036/- as against Rs.13,02,632/-, along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

17. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is Allowed In Part.
ii.

The impugned judgment and award dated 19.02.2011, passed in M.V.C.No.2044/2005, on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal & First Additional Senior Civil Judge And CJM, Mangalore is modified to the aforesaid extent.
